checks.name: Only the task emulator may run private pending-code lifecycle checks
Strict Android JSON parser accepts the complete device-pair contract
Starting a pair performs only its fixed native API request
Wrong-origin browser verification URL is rejected before any browser/cookie action
Malformed device secret cannot become a persisted pending login
Server cannot create an unbounded pending-code lifetime
Pending=true stays pending even if an unsolicited token field is present
An approved grant is accepted only after /api/session verifies the same server account
Grant identity verification uses only the own opaque bearer, never forum cookies
Cookie verification checks the same own session through the actual Cookie header path
A failed final cookie verification remains a failure and requires rollback, never connected UI
Mismatched grant/session user ids cannot produce a connected account
Invalid grant token is rejected before cookie creation
Expired grant is rejected before cookie creation
Missing explicit pending=false is not interpreted as successful authentication
A non-authenticated /api/session response cannot complete pairing
Revoked grant remains an authentication error rather than a fake connected state
Expired pending code remains distinguishable for explicit renewal
Rate limits remain distinguishable for bounded backoff
HTTP redirect is not followed into another authentication context
Rejected redirect causes no second transport request
Transient verification failure remains retryable
Controller receives one declared pending pair asynchronously
Pending code and expiry are committed to private app preferences
A fresh controller restores the same unexpired pending code and bounded remaining lifetime
Restoring a pending flow does not request another server/device code
Explicit cancellation clears pending device credentials
A stale retained controller cannot reopen a cancelled flow
Pending, restore and cancel do not alter the app's authenticated cookie
Short-lived declared pair is initially usable
Expired code is removed without an authenticated success
Expiry/return/process restore do not automatically issue or reopen a new login code
Only explicit new-code action renews an expired flow
Own /login opens the actual native pairing Activity instead of forum WebView
Real unauthenticated start API supplies one bounded pending code
Native flow retains the requested own room destination
Actual native Activity persists its unapproved code privately
Private pending credential and expiry follow the device API contract
Explicit native browser action creates an external intent
Browser receives the whole fixed-origin verification page in one browser context, with no partial OAuth URL
Native account Activity survives an actual configuration recreation
Rotation retains the in-flight controller rather than requesting another code
Rotation keeps the same private device code and never reopens the browser automatically
Recreated native login has actual window focus before system Back
Actual system Back cancels native pairing
Cancelling the native screen removes its pending credential
Cancelled pairing returns to the existing own app screen
Cancel shows an explicit sign-in/retry state rather than a generic network failure
Stale login page-start/page-finished callbacks do not reopen a cancelled flow
Own retry screen can be recreated after cancellation
Rotation/resume of the cancelled parent does not create an automatic login loop
Unapproved browser/pending/cancel lifecycle never fabricates an authenticated app cookie
Only an explicit native sign-in action reopens pairing after cancellation
Explicit retry has actual native window focus
Explicit retry remains cancellable without approving any account

scope: Declared bounded protocol fixtures; real native pairing/pending persistence/rotation/cancel and captured browser intent. No real forum login, approval, user credentials or synthetic connected account.
